prior_exception.reason: The defining 120 EC in years one and two is chemistry and laboratory centred: analytical, organic and inorganic chemistry; molecular structure and bonding; thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and physics; successive chemical synthesis and analysis laboratories. In year three, at least 12 EC of chemistry electives and a 12-EC independent chemistry research internship/report remain required. Although 27 EC can be freely chosen, UCR lacks a chemistry gateway and any stand-alone introductory or advanced organic, inorganic, analytical, physical or synthetic chemistry sequence. A 24-course UCR route using biology, geoscience, statistics and programming would have too little chemistry and would misrepresent the programme’s academic core.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official prospective year-one page is labelled 2027–28 while the year-two and year-three pages are indicative 2026–27; these are a present programme structure cross-check, not a guaranteed cohort contract. Summing positive-credit items yields 60 EC in each year. Year-three 9 EC taught compulsory work plus 12 EC compulsory internship plus 39 EC elective room = 60 EC; 12 of the latter is restricted to Chemistry electives, with 27 EC free. The education minor is optional, and alternative chemistry electives are not simultaneously required.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked all 151 enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, profile/topic enrichment, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biochemical content and molecular lab work, while HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 introduce life science and cells. ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical/inorganic processes and recovery; ENSSUST112 and ENSSUST211 address materials life cycles and energy systems. DISGATE102, DISMATH211/214/314 and DISGATE101 provide some mathematical, statistical and programming support. None provides the laboratory and theory progression in chemical analysis, organic/inorganic synthesis, physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and quantum chemistry required to underpin this bachelor and its independent chemistry research internship. Isolated biochemical and environmental chemistry coverage cannot support a defensible 24-course Chemistry match.

prior_exception.reason: This mathematics degree requires a broad proof-based progression: 51 EC in a dense first-year mathematical core, an additional required 6 EC multivariable analysis and 18 EC in differential equations, rings/fields and topology in the selected line, then 30 EC more upper mathematics (18 restricted line electives and 12 additional mathematics electives), plus a 12-EC independent mathematics thesis, seminar and modelling work. UCR offers introductory and applied mathematics, statistics, programming and data science but lacks sustained stand-alone real/complex analysis, abstract algebra and topology at the required depth. Substituting AI and data-science courses for the upper mathematical sequence would misrepresent the defining Mathematics identity, despite substantial overlap in applied computational methods.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The selected first-listed line is Mathematics, not the differently required Applied Mathematics or Probability and Statistics lines. Year 1=51 EC compulsory+9 EC free; years 2–3=12 EC common year-two courses+48 EC Mathematics line (18 prescribed, 18 restricted choices, 12 supplemental mathematics)+24 EC year-three fixed seminar/practicum/portfolio/thesis+36 EC genuinely free. The 3-EC first-listed course from the dedicated elective page meets its second-year selection rule. Exact elective allocations by year are illustrative and must respect the current online catalogue/OER. Public year-one/two pages give 2026–27 and year-three gives 2027–28 indicative offerings.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with descriptions, prerequisites, profiles and planned terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods introduces calculus and linear algebra; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics and DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics provide relevant but predominantly introductory or applied coverage. DISGATE101 Programming and DISDATA111/211/311 add computational/data-science methods. There is no dedicated UCR sequence in real and complex analysis, rings and fields, topology, functional analysis, number theory or mathematics-specific independent thesis sufficient for this 180-EC route. Cross-disciplinary electives cannot fill the restricted 48-EC Mathematics line without changing the subject of the comparison.

prior_exception.reason: The accessible current official VU prospectus is a thematic and partial course overview; it explicitly sends readers to the study guide for the complete programme. Individual VU 2026–27 course entries establish 60 EC of named components, but not the full compulsory sequence, the amount and restrictions of second-year free choice, the third-year minor/placement alternatives, or all third-year research-college credits. The applicable formal degree plan/OER is inaccessible to the available tools. Filling the other 120 EC or treating all displayed optional courses as mandatory would invent a 180-EC pathway. The UCR History response is academically plausible, but a fair lossless comparison must await a verified complete VU curriculum.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The generic Dutch-language Geschiedenis bachelor is the target; VU separately identifies History and International Studies and its different thesis/colloquium codes, which are not substituted here. The public History page describes the minor and the placement/abroad option without exact EC, and research-college topics rotate. The ten supported 2026–27 course credits listed sum to 60 EC; this partial subset does not purport to be a complete year or degree. Obtain the applicable 2026–27 study-guide degree structure or adopted OER and verify the choice space before reopening.
